Definition: middle voice from νοσφί (apart or clandestinely); to sequestrate for oneself, i.e. embezzle:--keep back, purloin.
BiblicalUsage: To keep back is to steal by halves, and Ananias does it with his wife's knowledge: he keeps back part of the price of the land and lays a certain part at the apostles' feet, and Peter calls it lying to the Holy Ghost. Paul tells servants the opposite: not purloining, but showing all good fidelity, that they may adorn the doctrine of God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the kept-back part is the whole sin: Ananias did not have to give it all, but having promised it, he lied about what he kept. Paul tells servants to show all good fidelity, that they may adorn the doctrine of God — the opposite of keeping back.
RelatedPeople: Simon Peter; Ananias, Husband of Sapphira
